description.narrative: (Uganda): With FY 2022 funds, Local Partner Health Services-TB will provide technical assistance to the National TB and HIV programs and support management of multidrug resistant TB (MDR-TB) across 17 treatment sites nationwide. It will also increase TB/HIV case detection and improve TB treatment outcomes through a health systems strengthening approach in the regions of Kampala, Wakiso, and Mukono.The activity will provide technical assistance to USAID implementing partners and focus districts to reduce Uganda's TB burden and contribute to the U.S. Government and World Health Organization's End TB Strategy, which seeks to end the TB epidemic by 2035. The activity works directly with Ministry of Health leadership to address Uganda's high TB burden and focuses on finding missing TB cases through effective community and facility-based interventions.The activity will partner with other USG-supported TB/HIV partners. Coordination includes: 1) providing support to the National TB Leprosy program to improve the quality of the current MDR-TB program; 2) developing and implementing strategies that mitigate impact of COVID-19; 3) increasing screening and detection of all forms of TB; 4) improving early treatment initiation and successful treatment completion; and 5) strengthening community systems to support the continuum of prevention, diagnosis, and treatment.LPHS-TB will fund activities to: 1) improve gender equality and empower women to access and use high quality health services; 2) improve gender equality and empower women to access and use high quality health services; and 3) prevent gender-based violence and address the impact of gender-based violence and activities to mitigate the impact of climate induced disruptions to the delivery of health services.These activities are jointly supported with PEPFAR (HIV) funds, and therefore, this activity is co-funded with HIV/PEPFAR funds for the HSS cross-cutting areas at subnational level...
